newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cenbank says 1997 M3 target 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cenbank says 1997 M3 target 18 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Slovenia said on Wednesday its target M3 growth for 1997 was 18 percent, down from 19.9 percent growth in the last year.
It said the target corridor would be 8 percentage points, placing M3 growth between 14 and 22 percent this year.

"The central bank is targeting the money aggregate on the assumption that it is connected to the inflation rate," Francek Drenovec, head of the sector of analysis and reasearch, told a news conference.
The bank said the target was in line with its policy to push Slovenia's inflation rate down towards Western European levels in the next couple of years.
"Our goal remains to keep Slovenian money stable with a long-term tendency of decreasing inflation," the central bank's governor France Arhar said.

The government said earlier it expected Slovenia's inflation rate to decrease to three percent by the year 2001. In 1997 inflation is expected to be unchanged or slightly below last year's 8.8 percent.

Arhar said the bank's long-term goal of reducing inflation would only be achieved if salary growth slowed and the state successfully undertook pension reform. The system relies almost entirely on public pensions.

The bank also said its target was based on the assumption that foreign exchange inflows would remain steady compared to last year, when foreign exchange inflows in the private sector amnounted to $530 million. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
